I and a group of friends are looking to try DnD for the first time. We are going through the rules and ran into an issue about keeping secrets between players.

An example might be, only one character in the group understands a certain language. Something is said in that language and that character may decide he or she wants to lie about what was said to the other characters.

Does the GM privately speak with the person who can understand the language every time? Do the players all hear what was said and then pretend their characters don't know? How would situations like these be handled?

That probably depends on your group of friends. The easiest way to handle it would be to write down what is said on a piece of paper, that way it can be shared between the GM and the players who would know what is being said.

If your group of friends can avoid meta-gaming situations (which would be when the player knows information the character would not, but acts upon it anyways), then you could say it out loud. If you believe your friends can handle keeping player knowledge and character knowledge separate, then this will save you the writing time.

For a group of new players, I would recommend the note passing though. It's good for all sorts of things, like having your character do something you don't want others to know(like always checking the corpses of your recently defeated foes first to pocket some extra gold) or keeping information secret.

I've heard some people skip the note passing step and go for texting that kind of information back and forth, but you'll find people getting distracted as soon as they pull their phones out!

Here here! Well put and I'll also say that phones during play can really put a damper on things if not done well. We use Google hangouts for secrets and stuff and it works well some times but other times it can lead into a long distraction.

I'll also say that for a group of new players in depth secrets may not be the best route as it can make things overly complicated. And the idea of one person having a little exchange with the DM privately can take away from the other players enjoyment of the game simply because they can't be a part of it.
